title: Synchronization & coordination primitives
literature: Little Book of Semaphores (Downey); Butenhof POSIX Threads; Herlihy & Shavit Art of Multiprocessor Programming; Java Concurrency in Practice; POSA2 concurrency patterns.

members.name: ABA Mitigation via Tagged Pointer
members.what: Pair the CAS-protected word with a monotonically increasing tag/version so a value that was changed and changed back still fails the CAS.

members.name: Acquire-Release Ordering
members.what: Pair a release-ordered store by the producer with an acquire-ordered load by the consumer so everything written before the release is visible after the acquire, without full fences.

members.name: Balking
members.what: A method that immediately returns (or reports failure) instead of waiting when the object is not in an appropriate state to execute the request.

members.name: Coarse-Grained Lock
members.what: Locks a group of related objects with a single lock (often a shared version object or a lock on an aggregate root) instead of locking each member.

members.name: Compare-and-Swap Loop
members.what: The nonblocking update idiom: read the current value, compute a new value, and atomically install it only if the location still holds the value read, retrying on failure.

members.name: Condition Variable
members.what: A queue on which threads wait, releasing an associated lock, until another thread signals that a state predicate may now hold; woken threads re-acquire the lock and re-test the predicate.

members.name: Coordinator
members.what: A coordinator drives a task spanning multiple participants through prepare and commit phases so either all participants complete their work or none do.

members.name: Critical Region
members.what: Making a code region atomic by disabling interrupts or task switching (or holding a global lock) for its duration.

members.name: Deadlock Detection
members.what: Maintain a waits-for graph of which transactions block which, periodically detect cycles, and break them by aborting a chosen victim (alternatives: timeouts, wound-wait/wait-die prevention).

members.name: Direct-to-Task Notification
members.what: Each task carries built-in notification slots (a 32-bit value plus pending state) that other tasks or ISRs can set, increment, overwrite, or OR bits into, letting the task block on its own notification instead of on a separate kernel object

members.name: Double-Checked Locking
members.what: Code checks a condition (typically 'initialized?') before and again after acquiring a lock, so the common already-initialized path skips locking entirely.

members.name: Event Flags Group
members.what: A kernel object holding a word of boolean event bits that tasks and ISRs set or clear atomically and that tasks block on with AND/OR combinations of bits, optionally auto-clearing the bits on wake.

members.name: Eventcount
members.what: A monotonically increasing counter that threads can read, advance, and await reaching a value, letting a lock-free fast path add blocking ('sleep until something changed') without locks.

members.name: Fencing Token
members.what: Attach a monotonically increasing token to each lock/lease grant; resources reject requests bearing a token older than one already seen, fencing off stale holders.

members.name: Flat Combining
members.what: Threads publish operation requests to a shared list; one thread acquires a global lock and applies everyone's pending operations in a batch on their behalf.

members.name: Futex
members.what: Synchronization objects keep their state in a plain userspace word manipulated with atomics; the kernel is invoked only to sleep on or wake waiters when the fast path fails.

members.name: Guarded Call
members.what: Cross-thread service invocation performed synchronously but guarded by a mutual-exclusion semaphore so only one caller executes the service at a time.

members.name: Guarded Suspension
members.what: A method that suspends the calling thread until a precondition (guard) over the object's state becomes true, then executes; the wait-loop-on-condition-variable pattern form.

members.name: Implicit Lock
members.what: Has framework or layer-supertype code acquire the needed offline locks automatically so application code cannot forget them.

members.name: Interrupt-Masking Critical Section
members.what: Protect data shared between mainline code and ISRs by briefly disabling (or priority-masking) interrupts around the access.

members.name: Latch
members.what: A one-shot synchronizer that blocks waiting threads until it reaches its terminal (open) state - typically when a count of prerequisite events reaches zero - and then stays open forever.

members.name: Lock Escalation
members.what: When a transaction holds too many fine-grained locks, the lock manager replaces them with a single coarser-granularity lock to cap lock-table memory.

members.name: Lock Striping
members.what: Partitioning a data structure's protection across an array of locks (e.g., one per hash-bucket group) so independent operations contend only on their stripe.

members.name: Logical Clock
members.what: A per-process counter (scalar or vector) advanced on local events and merged on message receipt so that timestamp order respects causal (happened-before) order without synchronized physical clocks.

members.name: MCS Queue Lock
members.what: Waiters enqueue a per-thread node and spin only on their own node's flag; the releaser hands the lock to its queue successor.

members.name: Memory Barrier
members.what: An explicit instruction or compiler directive that constrains the order in which memory operations before and after it may become visible to other processors.

members.name: Monitor Object
members.what: An object synchronizes its own method execution with an internal lock plus condition variables, so at most one method runs at a time and methods can wait for state conditions inside the object.

members.name: Multi-Granularity Locking
members.what: Locks are taken at multiple granularities (database, table, page, row) with intention modes (IS, IX, SIX) on ancestors advertising finer-grained locks below.

members.name: Multiversion Concurrency Control
members.what: Keep multiple timestamped versions of each data item so readers see a consistent older version while writers create new ones, with obsolete versions garbage-collected later.

members.name: Operational Transformation
members.what: Keep concurrently edited replicas consistent by transforming each incoming operation against the concurrent operations already applied locally, preserving intention and causality without locking.

members.name: Optimistic Concurrency Control
members.what: Proceed without locks, recording versions of the data read; at commit time re-check the versions and retry the whole operation if anything changed.

members.name: Optimistic Offline Lock
members.what: Prevents conflicts between concurrent business transactions by validating at commit time (typically via a version field) that no other session changed the data since it was read.

members.name: Ordered Locking
members.what: Every lockable resource gets a global order/ID and all tasks must acquire locks in strictly increasing order, making circular wait impossible.

members.name: Pessimistic Offline Lock
members.what: Prevents conflicts between concurrent business transactions by acquiring an application-managed lock on data before working with it, forcing other sessions to wait or be refused.

members.name: Priority Ceiling Protocol
members.what: Each resource is assigned a ceiling priority equal to the highest priority of any task that may lock it, and locking rules built on the ceilings bound blocking to one critical section and prevent deadlock.

members.name: Priority Inheritance Protocol
members.what: A task holding a lock temporarily inherits the highest priority of any task blocked on that lock, releasing the boost when it unlocks.

members.name: Read-Copy-Update
members.what: Readers traverse shared data with essentially zero synchronization while updaters publish new versions atomically and defer reclamation of old versions until all pre-existing readers have finished (a grace period).

members.name: Readers-Writer Lock
members.what: A lock admitting either many concurrent readers or one exclusive writer, exploiting the fact that reads do not conflict with each other.

members.name: Reentrant Lock
members.what: A mutex variant that the holding thread may re-acquire without deadlocking, tracked by owner and hold count; charter-noted as a variant of the plain mutex kept separate for its distinct semantics.

members.name: Rendezvous
members.what: An explicit synchronization object at which multiple tasks wait until a predetermined condition (e.g., all parties arrived) is met, then proceed together.

members.name: Safe Publication
members.what: The set of idioms (final fields, volatile references, locks, initialized statics, concurrent collections) that make an object and its state visible to other threads in a fully constructed form.

members.name: Safepoint
members.what: A designated point in generated or interpreted code at which a thread's state (GC roots, stack maps) is fully described and the thread can be safely blocked; the runtime brings all threads to safepoints (via polls, page-protection tricks, o

members.name: Scoped Locking
members.what: A guard object acquires a lock in its constructor and releases it in its destructor, so every exit path from a scope (including exceptions) releases the lock.

members.name: Self-Pipe Trick
members.what: A process writes a byte to a pipe it also polls, converting an asynchronous event (typically a signal) into a file-descriptor readiness event handled in the main event loop.

members.name: Semaphore
members.what: An integer counter with atomic wait (decrement-or-block) and signal (increment-and-wake) operations, used to control access to a pool of permits.

members.name: Sequence Lock
members.what: A writer increments a sequence counter before and after updating; readers retry their lock-free read if the counter was odd or changed across the read.

members.name: Simultaneous Locking
members.what: A task acquires all resources it will need in one atomic all-or-none step (releasing everything on partial failure), so it never holds some while waiting for others.

members.name: Snapshot Isolation
members.what: A transaction reads from a consistent snapshot taken at its start and commits only if no concurrent committed transaction wrote the same items (first-committer-wins).

members.name: Software Transactional Memory
members.what: Shared-memory operations grouped into transactions that execute optimistically and commit atomically, aborting and retrying on conflict, giving composable lock-free-style synchronization.

members.name: Spinlock
members.what: A lock acquired by busy-waiting (repeatedly testing an atomic flag) instead of blocking, trading CPU cycles for elimination of scheduler round-trips.

members.name: Strategized Locking
members.what: The synchronization mechanism a component uses is a pluggable strategy (template parameter or polymorphic lock object), including a null lock for single-threaded configurations.

members.name: Test-and-Test-and-Set Lock
members.what: Spin reading the lock word from cache until it appears free, and only then attempt the atomic test-and-set; typically combined with exponential backoff between attempts.

members.name: Thread Confinement
members.what: Restricting all access to mutable data to a single thread, making synchronization unnecessary for that data.

members.name: Thread-Safe Interface
members.what: Public interface methods acquire the component's lock and then delegate to non-locking private implementation methods; implementation methods never call locking interface methods.

members.name: Ticket Lock
members.what: A spinlock built from two counters: acquirers atomically take a ticket and spin until the now-serving counter reaches it.

members.name: Timestamp-Ordering Concurrency Control
members.what: Assign each transaction a unique timestamp at start and enforce that all conflicting reads and writes execute in timestamp order, aborting operations that arrive too late.

members.name: Two-Phase Locking
members.what: A locking discipline in which a transaction acquires all its locks before releasing any (growing then shrinking phase), which suffices to guarantee serializable executions.
